verdict.rationale: Twilio's Authy docs say it provides an SDK for common web languages as the fastest way to integrate 2FA without calling the Authy API directly. However, the runtime probe of the same docs page records that 'The Authy API is now closed to new customers and will be fully deprecated in the future', leaving no programmatic surface open to new integrations. Verify, the successor, is a separate product and is not credited here. Missing for 10: an SDK that new customers can actually build against, a list of supported languages, SDK reference documentation, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: So you don't have to use the Authy API directly to integrate two-factor authentication into your app, we provide an SDK for common web languages.
we provide an SDK for common web languages. If your language is supported, it's the fastest way to get started.
